_comment: Known-failing pytest tests (#4562). CI fails on any failure NOT listed here. Regenerate with: python scripts/check_pytest_baseline.py <junit.xml> --update. #5169, #5175, #5255, #5257, #5284, #5287, #5288, #5289, #5290, #5291, #5292, #5295, #5419, and #5225 removed obsolete or newly passing entries by hand, as did #5811 (38 entries: 36 tests that run and pass, and 2 that no longer exist — --strict-stale cannot see the latter): --strict-stale (#5091) fails the job on a baselined test that passes. #6657 removed 15 entries that only failed because CI had no `auralis_dsp` (they pass once the job builds it). #6708 removed 14 entries under tests/performance, tests/load_stress and tests/stress: those directories are marked slow and run only in the nightly slow-tests.yml job, so this per-push baseline can no longer see them pass or fail. #6598 removed 3 entries for tests/regression/test_frontend_hook_patterns.py, deleted in favour of behavioural vitest coverage. #6709 removed 11 entries that ran and passed in run 44944948134, the first completed run with auralis_dsp built (6 of them in test_cross_dimensional_interactions). #6709 follow-up removed the 2 test_data_migration TestUserPreferencesMigration entries: they asserted that add() keeps favorite/play_count, which only the scanner calls and a file never carries, and were rewritten to check the stats survive a rescan and a metadata edit. It also removed 4 entries that handed HybridProcessor.process() a file path (it takes decoded audio): those tests decode through tests/audio_processing.process_file now, and test_process_nonexistent_file became test_process_rejects_a_path_with_a_clear_error. Removed rather than regenerated -- a baseline built outside CI reports spurious new failures.
